articles.headline: Two men found guilty of helping Iran try to ‘eliminate’ UK-based journalists
articles.snippet: Mostafa Sepahvand and Farhad Javadi Manesh carried out surveillance in an effort to inflict violence on targets Two men of Iranian origin who were hired through social media as part of a plan to…

agreed_facts.text: Two Iranian men were convicted of spying in the UK.
The men carried out surveillance of journalists.
The case involved a violent element: one man was convicted of planning violence, and the surveillance aimed to inflict violence on targets.

headline_quotes.quote: helping Iran try to ‘eliminate’ UK-based journalists
hired through social media

emphasis.text: Names the two men and foregrounds the aim to 'eliminate' journalists. It says the men were hired through social media.

headline_quotes.quote: UK court convicts 2 Iranian men of spying on journalists
a Persian-language television station critical of Iran's government

emphasis.text: Leads with the court verdict and identifies the targets as reporters for a Persian-language TV station critical of Iran's government.

headline_quotes.quote: Iran's shadow operations stretch across Europe
chilling spy convictions expose Tehran's reach

emphasis.text: Places the convictions within wider Iranian activity abroad. It cites France accusing the IRGC of cyberattacks and UAE officials warning of Iranian sleeper cells.

omissions.text: The right-leaning coverage does not mention that the men's targets were journalists.
The right-leaning coverage does not mention the violent aim or the planning of violence.
The left-leaning coverage does not mention France's accusation of IRGC cyberattacks or UAE warnings of Iranian sleeper cells.
The centre coverage does not mention France's accusation of IRGC cyberattacks or UAE warnings of Iranian sleeper cells.

headline_quotes.quote: UK court convicts 2 Iranian men of spying on journalists
Two men found guilty of helping Iran try to ‘eliminate’ UK-based journalists
chilling spy convictions expose Tehran's reach

emphasis.text: Western coverage reports the convictions and the surveillance of journalists.
One outlet links the case to Iranian activity elsewhere in Europe and the UAE.

summary.text: Two Iranian men were convicted of spying in Britain. A London court found they surveilled journalists working for a Persian-language TV station critical of Iran's government. The Guardian names them as Mostafa Sepahvand and Farhad Javadi Manesh and says the surveillance aimed to inflict violence.

conclusion.text: All three outlets report that two Iranian men were convicted of spying in the UK. The centre and left outlets focus on journalists as targets and the violent aim. The right outlet frames the case as part of wider Iranian operations abroad. No claims are disputed between the outlets.
